palette.notes: Measured 19 colours with one long ramp (length 19, median hue shift 34.9 deg) on a compressed copy. Night scenes are teal-blue throughout; warm accents only on the red CAFE sign, tail lights and desk lamp. The last room scene shifts to a warm daylight grade.

lighting: Ambient night teal everywhere, with small warm local lights (lamp cone, tail lights, sign) as focal points; time of day is told by switching the whole scene's grade to warm daylight.
silhouette: Small chunky characters: tall dad, tiny kid in a red/pink top that pops against the teal; poses read through body shape, not faces.

motion.timing: Measured median hold 100 ms (p25 67, p75 100), on 3s, 4.45 drawings/s over the first 20 s: mostly still scenes with small loops (kid running, snow falling, typing).

texture: Clean pixels, almost no dither (0.0014); falling snow pixels and a subtle overlay give atmosphere.
camera: Locked-off wide tableau shots, one per scene, with fades from black and between scenes; no pans.

acting.enters: Fades in on dad and kid already in place by the car at night.
acting.acts: Dad stands; the kid runs around him, falls in the snow, gets up, then stands beside him: the kid carries the scene while dad holds.
acting.exits: Scene fades out and returns in a new place (a home office, dad at the computer, kid on the sofa).
acting.depth: Both characters sit small in a big detailed set, mid-ground, framed by props; the kid is the moving accent.

techniques: teal night grade with warm point lights as focal accents
one tableau per memory, cut by fades: same pair, new place
hold the big character still, let the small one move
time-of-day shift by regrading the same room night to day
warm-coloured clothing on the small hero to pop against a cool set
feel: cool teal sets + warm point lights + small held characters on 3s = nostalgic lofi memory
for_fred: Do a memory-montage beat: Fred and Pixie in the same pose in three tableaux (night, desk, sunny room), each a fade. Keep one still and let the other do a tiny loop; give the mover a warm colour against a cool set.
